entries.claim: The regular-file validation is still vulnerable to a meaningful TOCTOU race, so the original hang/resource-exhaustion blocker is not fully closed for concurrently operator-controlled paths.
entries.failure_scenario: An attacker/process can make CHANGELOG.md (or a symlink it follows) resolve to a regular file during statSync(), then replace it with a FIFO or point it at /dev/zero before readFileSync(). readFileSync() then opens the replacement and can again block indefinitely or consume unbounded memory before the promised unreadable-changelog refusal. Validate the opened descriptor (open first, fstat it, then read that descriptor), rather than validating the pathname and reopening it later.

counter_evidence.note: The prescribed remedy does not close what it names: open(2) on a FIFO with no writer BLOCKS in the open call itself, so openSync-then-fstatSync moves the indefinite hang from read to open rather than removing it, and only O_NONBLOCK would avoid that - which the finding does not propose. The race also needs an actor with write access to the working tree release-bump is bumping and about to commit, who can already substitute the manifest, the changelog body or the commit itself; a hang is strictly less than what that actor already holds, so it is not a high on this seam's threat model.
